mainTopic: How partners stand on חזקה, payment for improving shared land, and testimony, according to שמואל's rules about a שותף.
overview: The גמרא opens with two versions of a teaching. אבוה דשמואל and לוי say a שותף (partner) cannot establish חזקה, and an אומן (craftsman) certainly cannot. שמואל agrees about the craftsman but says a partner can, which fits his rule that partners count as separate parties. רבי אבא points out that שמואל also said a partner is like a יורד ברשות (someone who entered with permission), which seems to mean no חזקה. The first answer splits the cases into using the whole field versus half of it, and people apply this split in opposite directions. רבינא answers instead that in both cases the partner used the whole field, and the difference is whether the field is big enough to be divided. The גמרא then studies the יורד ברשות statement on its own and explains that it is about payment, not חזקה: a partner who improves the field collects from the fully grown improvement. Finally, the גמרא turns to שמואל's next rule, that partners may testify for each other.

steps.title: A partner has no presumption of ownership, and a craftsman certainly does not
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל and לוי teach that a שותף cannot establish חזקה, and an אומן all the more so cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל's father and לוי taught: A partner does not have a presumption of ownership, and all the more so a craftsman does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a teaching from אבוה דשמואל and לוי: a partner cannot use his possession of shared property to prove he owns it, and a craftsman surely cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partner has a right to be on the property, so his using it proves nothing about owning it outright. A craftsman holding an item is even weaker, because he received it only to fix it. That is why the teaching says 'all the more so' about the craftsman.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed ownership based on holding or using property
A partner, co-owner of property
A craftsman who holds an item to work on it
All the more so

phrases.english: Gemara:
Shmuel's father and Levi taught:
A partner does not have a presumption of ownership,
and all the more so a craftsman does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's rule about who cannot establish חזקה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither a שותף nor an אומן can establish חזקה.

steps.title: שמואל's version: a craftsman cannot, but a partner can
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches a different version: an אומן has no חזקה, but a שותף does.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל teaches: A craftsman does not have a presumption of ownership, but a partner does have a presumption of ownership.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with his father and לוי about the partner. He agrees that a craftsman cannot establish ownership, but he holds that a partner can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree about the אומן. The only dispute is the שותף. To שמואל, a partner who acts as sole owner can create a real חזקה against his fellow partner.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches (a version of a tannaitic teaching)
He has the ability to establish presumed ownership

phrases.english: Shmuel teaches:
A craftsman does not have a presumption of ownership,
but a partner does have a presumption of ownership.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version that disagrees with step 1 about the partner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אומן has no חזקה, but a שותף does.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions agree about the craftsman. They argue only about the partner: אבוה דשמואל and לוי say no חזקה, and שמואל says yes.

steps.title: שמואל is consistent: partners are treated as separate parties
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שמואל's view matches another statement of his: partners can establish חזקה against each other, testify for each other, and are שומרי שכר for each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל follows his own reasoning, as שמואל says: Partners establish a presumption of ownership against each other, testify for each other, and become paid guardians for each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל's view fits another rule of his. Elsewhere he treats partners as separate people in several ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If partners can testify for each other and act as paid guardians for each other, then שמואל sees each partner as an independent party. That is why one partner can also establish חזקה against the other.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own line of reasoning
They establish presumed ownership against one another
They testify
Paid guardians, who carry greater responsibility for the property

phrases.english: And Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
as Shmuel says:
Partners establish a presumption of ownership against each other,
and they testify for each other,
and they become paid guardians for each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 by showing it fits שמואל's wider view of partners.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that a שותף has חזקה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own statement that partners establish חזקה against each other, testify for each other, and are שומרי שכר for each other

steps.title: רבי אבא raises a contradiction from another statement of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא asks רב יהודה how שמואל can hold that a שותף has חזקה, when שמואל also said a שותף is like a יורד ברשות. That seems to mean he has no חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא raised a contradiction to רב יהודה in the cave of רב זכאי's house: Did שמואל really say a partner has a presumption of ownership? But didn't שמואל say a partner is like one who entered with permission? Isn't that saying a partner has no presumption of ownership?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges the version in step 2. He quotes a different statement of שמואל that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who enters a field with permission, like a sharecropper, cannot claim ownership from using it, because he was allowed to be there. If שמואל compares a partner to such a person, it seems a partner cannot establish חזקה either. That contradicts step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him
One who enters a field with permission
Isn't that to say

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised a contradiction to Rav Yehuda
in the cave of Rav Zakkai's house:
Did Shmuel really say:
A partner has a presumption of ownership?
But didn't Shmuel say:
A partner is like one who entered with permission.

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְמֵימְרָא דְּשׁוּתָּף אֵין לוֹ חֲזָקָה?
phrases.english: Isn't that saying a partner has no presumption of ownership?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's view from steps 2 and 3 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a שותף has חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל compares a partner to a יורד ברשות, who cannot establish ownership. So a partner should have no חזקה either, which contradicts step 2.

steps.title: Using the whole field versus using half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's two statements deal with different cases: one where the partner used the whole field and one where he used half.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where he went into all of the field, and that case is where he went into half of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each statement of שמואל deals with a different case: using the whole field or using only half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's two statements no longer clash, because each one fits a different way the partner used the field. The answer does not yet say which case gets חזקה and which does not. The next step deals with that.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the statements do not really contradict
He went into (used) the whole field
To half

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this is where he went into all of it,
that is where he went into half of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's two statements contradict each other about a partner's חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: One statement is about a partner who used the whole field and the other is about one who used half, so they do not contradict.

steps.title: The split can be applied in either direction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that some apply the whole-versus-half split one way, and some apply it the opposite way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way, and some say it the other way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that people disagree about which case gets חזקה. Some say using half creates חזקה and using the whole field does not, and others say the reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says that using exactly half looks like he is claiming that half as his own share, while using the whole field is just normal partner behavior. The other side says that using half proves nothing, but taking over the whole field, including his partner's half, does create חזקה. Either way, שמואל's two statements fit two different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say it
In this direction, this way

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not take sides. It tells you that the answer in step 5 works whichever way you assign 'whole field' and 'half field' to חזקה or no חזקה.

phrases.english: Some say it this way,
and some say it the other way.
phrases.notes: One way: half gives חזקה and the whole field does not. The other way: the whole field gives חזקה and half does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ לְהַאי גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies how to apply the answer given in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole-versus-half split can be applied in either direction.

steps.title: רבינא: the difference is whether the field can be divided
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers differently. In both cases the partner used the whole field, and the difference is whether the field is big enough for דין חלוקה (forced division).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Both this and that are where he went into the whole field, and it is not difficult. This case is where the field is big enough to be divided, and that case is where it is not big enough to be divided.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a new answer to רבי אבא's contradiction. The question is not how much of the field the partner used, but whether the field is big enough to be split between the partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field can be divided, each partner could demand his own half. So a partner who uses the whole field, including his partner's half, is acting like an owner and establishes חזקה. If the field is too small to divide, it stays shared, so using all of it is just normal partner behavior. Then he is like a יורד ברשות and has no חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that
The law that a field big enough for each partner to get a usable share can be split on demand
It does not have

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction in שמואל. The first splits the cases into the whole field versus half of it. רבינא's answer: both cases involve the whole field, and a partner gets חזקה only if the field is big enough to be divided.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא ties a partner's חזקה to whether the partnership could have been split. If it could be split, using the whole field means he is treating his partner's share as his own.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Both this and that are where he went into the whole field;
and it is not difficult:
this is where the field is big enough to be divided,
that is where it is not big enough to be divided.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הָא וְהָא דִּנְחֵית לְכוּלַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction in step 4, replacing the whole-versus-half split from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by a different factor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements of שמואל seem to clash about a partner's חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In both cases the partner used the whole field. If the field can be divided, he has חזקה; if it cannot, he is like a יורד ברשות and has none.

steps.title: Going back to שמואל's statement about a partner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again שמואל's statement that a שותף is like a יורד ברשות, so it can study that statement on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself: שמואל said that a partner is treated like someone who goes into a field with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is returning to a statement it mentioned earlier in passing, so it can examine it closely. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבי אבא used this statement of שמואל to raise a difficulty. Now the גמרא looks at the statement for its own sake. The open question is what being 'like a יורד ברשות' actually means for a partner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to a statement quoted earlier in order to discuss it directly
A partner, a co-owner of property
Someone who goes into another person's field with the owner's permission

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: This is the statement רבי אבא quoted back in step 4. Now the גמרא studies it directly.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A partner is considered like one who enters with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's יורד ברשות statement, which רבי אבא quoted in step 4, so the גמרא can study it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A partner is treated like someone who entered the field with permission.

steps.title: Why didn't שמואל just say a partner has no חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל's wording adds. If he only meant that a partner cannot make a חזקה, he should have said exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is שמואל teaching us here? That partnership gives no חזקה? Then he should simply have said: 'A partner has no חזקה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that 'like a יורד ברשות' just means 'a partner has no חזקה.' If that were the point, the wording is a roundabout way to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רבי אבא's contradiction assumed this statement means a partner has no חזקה. Now the גמרא asks about the wording itself: if that were the message, שמואל would have said it plainly. The roundabout wording suggests the statement teaches something else, and step 10 says what.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is he teaching us?': asking what new point a statement adds
A claim of ownership based on using the property for a set time
'Let him say': if that were his point, he should have said it directly

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas here. 'No חזקה' is about proving ownership. The גמרא is about to show that 'like a יורד ברשות' is really about how a partner gets paid for improving the field.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us,
that in partnership there is no presumption of ownership?
Then let him say: A partner has no presumption of ownership!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the meaning of the statement just quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that שמואל's יורד ברשות statement simply means a partner has no חזקה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the only message were 'no חזקה,' שמואל would have said that directly. The roundabout wording must teach something different.

steps.title: The real point: a partner collects his share of the full grown improvement
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, explains that שמואל meant a partner who improves the field collects from the fully grown improvement. This holds even in a field not usually planted, just like in a field that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: שמואל meant that the partner takes from the improvement that has grown to the point of being carried on the shoulders. In a field not normally used for planting, he collects just as he would in a field that is normally planted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: שמואל's statement is not about חזקה at all. It is about how much a partner gets paid for improving the shared field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a partner counts as someone who entered 'with permission,' he is not treated like an intruder who planted without asking. So he shares in the full grown improvement, which the text describes as ready to carry on the shoulders. This applies even when the field is not the kind people usually plant.

keyTerms.meaning: The improvement, the added value from the work done
'Reaching the shoulders': produce fully grown and ready to harvest and carry
A field normally used for planting trees

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'a partner is like a יורד ברשות' is about payment for improvements, not about חזקה. The partner collects from the fully grown improvement, whatever kind of field it is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer turns a statement that looked like a rule about חזקה into a rule about money owed for improving shared property. A partner who invests in the shared field is protected.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
It comes to say that he takes from the improvement
that reaches the shoulders,
phrases.notes: The produce is fully grown, ready to be cut and carried away on someone's shoulders.

phrases.english: in a field that is not usually used for planting,
just as in a field that is usually used for planting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by giving שמואל's statement a new meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the statement is about payment for improvements, not about חזקה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Like a יורד ברשות' just means a partner cannot make a חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a partner who improved the field collects from the fully grown improvement, even in a field not usually planted.

steps.title: Next part of שמואל's statement: partners testify for each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of שמואל's earlier statement, that partners may testify for each other, in order to discuss it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And partners may testify for one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next part of שמואל's statement from step 3 and brings it up for discussion. This line sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3, שמואל listed three rules about partners: they can make חזקה against each other, they can testify for each other, and they are שומרי שכר for each other. Having dealt with חזקה, the גמרא now turns to the second rule. Testifying for each other is surprising, because a partner seems to have a personal stake in the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: They testify for each other

phrases.english: And they testify for each other.
phrases.notes: This is the second rule from שמואל's list back in step 3. The גמרא is about to discuss it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the יורד ברשות discussion, the גמרא returns to שמואל's list from step 3 and takes up its second clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partners may testify for one another.
